correctness.rationale: Uniform parity vertices have covariance I and lie on the N-radius-squared sphere, so a trace-determinant argument uniquely forces the Löwner ball. The optimal support sign reversal loses exactly twice the least Gaussian absolute coordinate on a violated block, yielding an exact half-normal integral formula for width. A strictly positive integral second difference proves extremal partitions. Opposite-direction sign parity yields the even/odd law; exponential minimum convergence with bounded moments and the triangular-array Lyapunov theorem give the stated fixed-k and growing-k limits. Direct exhaustive feasible-vertex and support-function computations corroborated all finite formulas on eleven profiles and 176 test directions; the arbitrary-dimensional theorem is analytic.
